pre-fix-yarn.meaning: "a bit of rain in the current forecast" narrows precipitation to rain and adds a small amount; the dates, limits, temperature threshold and handling instructions otherwise remain.
pre-fix-yarn.sense: "land yer fish quick smart" correctly calls for quick landing, and "come good before you let 'em go" retains recovery before release.
pre-fix-yarn.authenticity: "Don't play hooked trout till they're stuffed" and "quick smart" are plausible broad Australian instructions.
pre-fix-yarn.register: "Anglers'll be right", "cos", "yer" and "come good" sustain broad level-5 body prose while avoiding added openers and keeping within the vulgarity cap.
pre-fix-yarn.tone: "The restrictions and closures had to go in" and "Don't play hooked trout" keep the conservation warning and instruction serious beneath the slang.
pre-fix-yarn.flow: "Depending on how the conditions shape up, the temporary restrictions might come off, or more closures could go in" is clear aloud.
pre-fix-yarn.variety: "wound back", "knock fish off", "quick smart" and "come good" vary the idiom across the repeated notice structure.
pre-fix-yarn.essence: "from sunup till 2 p.m. each day" and "let 'em come good before you let 'em go" preserve the successive updates and fish-protection purpose.

current.meaning: "there's rain in the current forecast" specifies rain where the source says precipitation; the operative dates, hours, scope and fish-care instructions otherwise survive.
current.sense: "wet a line" fits fishing and "head off the need" correctly renders preventing a future prohibition.
current.authenticity: "Don't play hooked trout till they're knackered" and "Doing your bit" are natural Australian phrasing.
current.register: "Staff will keep tabs" and "wet a line" add local idiom, but much of the eligible prose remains a moderate conversational notice rather than the requested broad level 5.
current.tone: "The restrictions and closures were needed" preserves their necessity and the conservation purpose.
current.flow: "When conditions picked up, that was eased back to partial restrictions on Aug. 28" is smoothly sequenced and easy to follow.
current.variety: "wet a line" and "Staff will keep tabs" recur in the two updates, but "Doing your bit" and "head off" provide some range.
current.essence: "let them recover before release" retains the core handling instruction and the dual-update notice structure.

dinkum-3.meaning: "every creek that runs into 'em" narrows tributaries to creeks, and "give 'em a chance to come good" weakens the instruction to let fish recover before release.
dinkum-3.sense: "got wound back to part-day restrictions" correctly captures the eased closures; "knackered" fits exhaustion.
dinkum-3.authenticity: "fishos", "Do us a favour" and "land yer fish quick" are credible Australian vernacular.
dinkum-3.register: "Good news for fishos:" and "mind" add disabled opening/tag garnish, despite the otherwise appropriate broad body voice.
dinkum-3.tone: "Don't play a hooked trout till it's knackered" retains the warning and care for fish in colloquial terms.
dinkum-3.flow: "With the weather and the water coolin' off, and a bit of rain in the forecast too, the full closures can come off" is readily spoken.
dinkum-3.variety: "Staff'll keep an eye on the water temperatures" and "Depending on how things are lookin'" repeat the same formula across updates.
dinkum-3.essence: "from sunup till 2 p.m. each day" and "ban fishin' at all hours" preserve the two stages of restrictions and their protective rationale.

pre-fix-yarn.quote: a bit of rain in the current forecast
pre-fix-yarn.original: precipitation in the current weather forecast
pre-fix-yarn.why: Rain is narrower than precipitation, and a bit adds an amount not stated.

current.quote: there's rain in the current forecast
current.original: precipitation in the current weather forecast
current.why: This narrows the forecast type without support.

current.quote: Staff will keep tabs on the water temperatures.
current.original: Staff will continue to monitor the water temperatures.
current.why: Representative of a relatively light-to-moderate local voice across eligible prose, noticeably below the broad level-5 brief.

current.quote: Anglers will be able to wet a line
current.original: Anglers will be able to fish
current.why: Wet a line is reused in the later update, as is keep tabs; the repeated choices make the voice a little less varied.

dinkum-3.why: Tributaries may be rivers as well as creeks, so the scope becomes narrower.

dinkum-3.quote: a bit of rain in the forecast
dinkum-3.original: precipitation in the current weather forecast
dinkum-3.why: Adds an amount and narrows precipitation to rain.

dinkum-3.quote: give 'em a chance to come good before ya let 'em go
dinkum-3.why: Giving fish a chance does not require waiting until they have recovered, weakening a protective instruction.
Added opener and the later mind tag violate disabled garnish.

dinkum-3.quote: Depending on how things are lookin'
dinkum-3.why: The same phrasing recurs in both monitoring paragraphs, alongside a repeated keep an eye formula.

summaries.pre-fix-yarn: The strongest broad-voice fit, with the practical rules and conservation instructions intact apart from a small weather-detail shift.
summaries.current: Clear and careful in substance, but substantially lighter in Australian weight than requested.
summaries.dinkum-3: Broad and natural, but disabled garnish and weakened precision in scope and fish recovery reduce its suitability.
